claims.statement: 186 orders allocated overnight are stuck in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' state since ~06:00 on east-node lanes
claims.limitation: State confirmed; underlying cause not yet identified

claims.statement: All stuck orders were routed to east node and flagged as 'split-reservation exceptions' by the overnight allocator
claims.limitation: Flag indicates unusual behavior; mechanism unknown

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 deployed at 22:00 reserves stock from east node first for multi-node orders; deployment review passed and regression suite was green
claims.limitation: Regression suite tested in controlled environment; live behavior may differ

claims.statement: The v18 change and stuck-order onset are temporally associated (v18 at 22:00, orders stuck from ~06:00); stuck orders are all on east-node lanes, which is the target of the v18 change
claims.limitation: Temporal correlation and split-reservation exception flag suggest causation, but require evidence to rule out coincidence

claims.statement: Inventory Control reported allocation totals reconcile and observability cannot correlate booked pickup with carrier confirmation
claims.limitation: Observability gap prevents carrier-side visibility; cannot rule out carrier-side issue or pickup scheduling failure

next_action.rationale: The 'split-reservation exception' flag on all held orders is the highest-information diagnostic. It signals the v18 rule-set change is triggering non-standard allocation behavior. Auditing these exceptions will determine whether the issue is in v18's logic, east-node inventory state, or pickup scheduling. This is the narrowest diagnostic to confirm or eliminate v18 as the root cause before considering rollback or escalation.
